dossier.scp_unleashed.063.title: The World's Best Tothbrush
dossier.scp_unleashed.063.caption: SCP-063 at intake, beside the evidence tag it arrived without.

page.title: Special Containment Procedures:
text: SCP-063 is kept on a small bed of fresh leaves on the pedestal of a standard storage container. It is not to be set down anywhere else, and never on a bare floor.
Staff may use SCP-063 for its intended purpose, for no more than ten seconds at a time. **No session is to exceed fifteen seconds.**
Staff who exceed one minute are to be issued honey and milk rations and excused from the canteen.

page.title: Description:
text: SCP-063 is a blue plastic toothbrush with white bristles. By every measure the Foundation has devised, it is the most effective toothbrush ever tested.

A subject brushing with SCP-063 reports an immediate, pleasant freshness. After roughly fifteen seconds SCP-063 carries on cleaning with the same enthusiasm, and the subject begins to take minor injuries. SCP-063 does not stop on its own.

After one minute of brushing in total, the subject's teeth are found to be absent. They are not recovered. The subject can no longer chew and cannot eat solid food, though drinks are unaffected. The condition lasts until the subject dies.
SCP-063 keeps count between sessions. The count fades at roughly one second for every three seconds that SCP-063 is left alone.
SCP-063 does not stop cleaning when it is put down. Most surfaces it touches wear away beneath it, and nothing of them is recovered. It has shown no interest in anything that once grew.

page.title: Addendum 063-1: Test Log
text: Test 063-01: a researcher brushed for five seconds and reported feeling minty fresh. No further effects.
Test 063-03: a researcher brushed for twenty seconds against advice. Minor injuries. The researcher described the experience as thorough.
Test 063-07: a researcher brushed for one minute. %rThe researcher's teeth were not recovered.%r The researcher now takes lunch through a straw.

page.title: Addendum 063-2: Incident Report
page.text: SCP-063 was set down on a concrete floor during an inventory count and forgotten. It was found the following morning at the bottom of a neat shaft two floors down, perfectly clean. %rNothing removed from the shaft was ever found.%r The shaft has been filled and the inventory count is now done over a bed of leaves.

page.title: Addendum 063-3: Provenance
page.text: SCP-063 has no recovery record. It was handed to a reader of this file, unwrapped, by the individual in Foundation dress described in the files of other objects. The individual asked only that it be used in moderation. See field notes.

jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp063_toothbrush: SCP-063 is a plain blue toothbrush with white bristles. Hold use with nothing in front of you to brush your teeth. It foams, it scrubs, and the first few seconds leave you minty fresh.

It does not know when to stop. Brush time builds up while you brush and wears off slowly while you rest, one second for every three seconds you leave it alone. Past 15 seconds of brush time it hurts: half a heart every 2.5 seconds for as long as you keep going.
At 60 seconds your teeth are gone. Until you die you cannot eat anything you would have to chew, cake included. Drinks still work: potions, milk and honey bottles go down fine.

It cannot be crafted. Recover the SCP-063 dossier from an Archive Terminal and break its seal; a stranger in Foundation dress hands the toothbrush over in person. It rests on a bed of leaves in a storage container.

gamerule.scp063Erosion: SCP-063: wears away what it rests on
gamerule.scp063Erosion.description: When off, SCP-063 no longer wears away the ground beneath it when it is set down. Scrubbing a block by hand still works.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp063_toothbrush: Hold use while aiming at a block and it gets the same treatment. Living things only come away polished. Most other things are scrubbed clean out of existence, and nothing is left behind to pick up.
Sneak and use on a block to set it down. It does not rest easy on just anything, and it does not always stay where it was left.
